subject: Biology
description: Light + dark reactions, chlorophyll, C3/C4 plants

questions.stem: The overall equation of PHOTOSYNTHESIS is:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (using chlorophyll). Reverse reaction is cellular respiration. Site: chloroplasts (thylakoids for light reactions, stroma for Calvin cycle).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Which part of the plant cell is the SITE of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chloroplast — double-membrane organelle; contains chlorophyll + stacks of thylakoid discs (grana). Light reactions on thylakoid membrane → ATP + NADPH + O₂. Calvin cycle (dark reactions) in stroma → glucose. Origin: endosymbiont theory (cyanobacterial ancestor).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The PRIMARY PIGMENT that captures light energy in photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll-a — primary photosynthetic pigment, the 'reaction centre' (P680, P700) that directly converts light to chemical energy. Chlorophyll-b, carotenoids (carotene, xanthophyll) are ACCESSORY pigments — absorb light and pass energy to chl-a.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The OXYGEN released during photosynthesis comes from:
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water (H₂O → 4 H⁺ + O₂ + 4 e⁻) on the thylakoid — oxygen released is the byproduct. Proved by Robin Hill (Hill reaction) + Sam Ruben / Martin Kamen isotope-labelling experiments (¹⁸O-labelled water gave ¹⁸O₂). H₂O, via photolysis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The DARK reactions of photosynthesis (Calvin-Benson cycle) take place in the:
questions.explanation: Calvin cycle (light-independent) — stroma. Uses ATP + NADPH (from light reactions) to fix CO₂ into 3-carbon compounds and eventually glucose. Discovered by Melvin Calvin (Nobel 1961, using ¹⁴C tracers).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: C4 plants (like maize, sugarcane) have an advantage over C3 plants (like wheat, rice) in:
questions.explanation: C4 plants — use PEP carboxylase to concentrate CO₂ near RuBisCO; reduce photorespiration (common in C3 at high temp). Bundle-sheath anatomy (Kranz anatomy). Examples: maize, sugarcane, sorghum, millets. CAM plants (cacti, pineapple) — capture CO₂ at night to save water. they lose less water and use CO₂ more efficiently.

questions.stem: The pores on the underside of leaves through which CO₂ enters and O₂ exits are called:
questions.explanation: Stomata — tiny pores flanked by GUARD CELLS that control opening/closing. Gas exchange + transpiration happen here. Lenticels — pores on woody stems. Cuticle — waxy outer layer preventing water loss. Most stomata on lower leaf surface to reduce evaporation.
